output.answer_markdown: In the FY2023 passage [6], SG&A fell to 23.5% of net sales from 23.9% in the comparison year. The passage calls that year "fiscal 2021". It attributes the decline primarily to lower marketing expenses and leverage of incentive compensation on higher sales. Deleverage of corporate overhead (strategic investments) and of store payroll and benefits (wage investments) partially offset these gains [6].
